title: Choose the Run of Show dashboard composition
question: All three keep the same Hackathons @ Berkeley identity. Choose the layout that should become the measured implementation contract.

options.label: Open binder
options.thesis: One broad active-work sheet and a narrow next-cues rail make the daily job unmistakable.
options.viewport: A blue mast frames a large application sheet beside a compact run-of-show rail.
options.risk: The familiar information split needs precise details to avoid reading as an ordinary dashboard.

options.label: Cue strip
options.thesis: A dominant numbered cue sequence turns application progress into the event's live production order.
options.viewport: A horizontal four-step cue dominates the mast above a focused logistics sheet.
options.risk: The wide sequence must collapse carefully on small screens.

options.label: Layered roles
options.thesis: Four staggered application sheets make the multi-role account model visible at a glance.
options.viewport: The active hacker sheet pulls forward while three role sheets remain visibly queued behind it.
options.risk: The strongest concept is also the hardest to preserve responsively without crowding.
